1. Validate the current bill: confirm meter reads imply 627 kWh (68,865 − 68,238), line items sum to $123.97 ($18.79 + $21.80 + $83.38), and the change versus last month is −$63.42 ($123.97 − $187.39); flag any arithmetic mismatch as a suspected billing error.

2. Map both billing periods to AEP Ohio tariffs by date: last month (2026-08-10 to 2026-09-09) and current (2026-09-09 to 2026-10-10) both fall under the post-2026-04-10 tariff (fixed $18.788; blended first-tier rate $0.1677638/kWh), so compute price_usd from any tariff difference applied to baseline usage (expected $0).

3. Compute days_usd from the period length change (30 days → 31 days), valuing the extra day at the household’s baseline daily cost or prorated fixed charge.

4. Estimate weather_usd from NOAA degree days: compare last month (CDD 296.5 / HDD 0) to current (CDD 120 / HDD 79), derive a weather-to-kWh coefficient from the bill history, convert the weather-driven kWh difference to dollars at the effective rate, or set weather_usd = 0 if no defensible coefficient can be estimated.

5. Compute usage_usd as the residual so price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd equals exactly −$63.42; separately model the current bill under the tariff and compare to $123.97 to set billing_error_suspected and billing_error_usd (expected false / null if within rounding).

6. Return only the JSON object with keys price_usd, days_usd, weather_usd, usage_usd, billing_error_suspected, and billing_error_usd.
